intro.title: Parent Respect & Connection Calculator
intro.body: Start with your real situation — distance, contact, life stage. Take a quick check or full depth. Get a gentle profile on presence, listening, and emotional balance. Everything stays in your browser.

setup.title: Your situation with your parents
setup.subtitle: This tunes prompts and insights — not a score on your love.
setup.contactLabel: How you usually stay in touch
setup.stageLabel: Where they are in life right now

distance.farAway: Far away — flights or long drives

contact.daily: Most days — calls, texts, or visits

stage.independent: Mostly independent — active on their own
stage.someHelp: Some help needed — errands, health, home
stage.caregiving: I'm a primary caregiver or very involved

result.caption: Honest parent-connection profile
result.shareText: My parent-respect profile: {{profile}} ({{score}}%). {{insight}} | Parent Respect — DailyLogic

profiles.steady-honor: Steady honor — presence you can build on
profiles.present-enough: Present enough — with room to deepen
profiles.learning-balance: Learning balance — good intent, messy life
profiles.good-intent: Good intent — now match it with rhythm
profiles.gap-to-close: A gap to close — not a moral failure
profiles.guilt-heavy: Guilt-heavy — time to trade shame for a plan
profiles.thin-contact: Thin contact — connection wants a slot
profiles.rebuild-gently: Rebuild gently — one visit, one call
profiles.pause-and-plan: Pause and plan — honor without burnout
profiles.start-small: Start small — respect grows in inches

insights.dim-presence-high: Your presence lands: they can feel you in the calendar, not only in speeches.
insights.dim-presence-low: Presence is the leak — not love. Pick one fixed slot they can predict.
insights.dim-listening-high: You listen like family: room for their story without rushing to fix.
insights.dim-listening-low: Listening wants practice — less advice, more curiosity on the first pass.
insights.dim-emotionalBalance-high: You hold boundaries and warmth together — that's mature kibbud without self-erasure.
insights.dim-emotionalBalance-low: Balance wobbles — guilt or resentment may be driving more than choice.
insights.overall-strong: The picture is strong: honoring without pretending it's effortless.
insights.overall-steady: Human steadiness — real care with normal blind spots.
insights.overall-developing: Real care, uneven habits — small rituals will move the needle.
insights.overall-needs-care: This asks for kindness to yourself and one concrete step this week.
insights.distance-sameArea: Living nearby is a gift — use it for quality, not only logistics and guilt trips.
insights.distance-shortDrive: A short drive can be a rhythm — batch errands with unhurried time together.
insights.distance-farAway: Distance makes intention visible — protect visit dates like meetings you don't cancel.
insights.stage-independent: They're still their own people — honor autonomy, not only worry.
insights.stage-someHelp: Help lands best when you ask what they want, not what you assume.
insights.stage-caregiving: Caregiving is heavy — respect includes protecting your own floor.
insights.contact-daily: Daily touch can drift into autopilot — keep one moment that's actually attentive.
insights.contact-fewWeekly: A few solid touchpoints beat scattered pings — make one of them undivided.
insights.contact-weekends: Weekend-only rhythm works if it's reliable — not only when you're free.
insights.contact-mostlyPhone: Phone can be real presence — voice, silence, and no multitasking count.

tips.tip-fixed-slot: Block one recurring slot (Tuesday walk, Sunday call) — predictability is respect.
tips.tip-voice-note: Send a 30-second voice note when you can't talk — tone carries more than a emoji.
tips.tip-shared-errand: Pair a chore they need with time together — pharmacy plus coffee, not drive-by duty.
tips.tip-two-questions: Open with two real questions before sharing your news — let them lead.
tips.tip-phone-walk: Take one call on a walk without screens — they'll hear the difference.
tips.tip-no-advice-first: When they vent, reflect once before suggesting fixes — honor the feeling first.
tips.tip-guilt-budget: Set a guilt budget: one act of repair, then move to plan — shame doesn't visit.
tips.tip-boundary-script: Write one sentence for boundaries: "I can't Tuesday, I can Thursday at six."
tips.tip-sibling-huddle: If siblings share load — a 20-minute huddle beats silent scorekeeping.
tips.tip-sunday-check: Sunday two-line check: "What's hard this week? What would help?"
tips.tip-visit-ritual: Far away? Pick a visit ritual — same meal, same photo walk — so trips feel anchored.
tips.tip-doorstep-coffee: Nearby? Ten-minute doorstep coffee beats a monthly marathon visit.

show-up-consistently.prompt: When I say I'll visit or stop by, I follow through on a rhythm my parents can rely on.

byDistance.sameArea: When I say I'll drop by locally, I actually show up — not only in a crisis.
byDistance.shortDrive: When I plan a drive to see them, I keep a visit rhythm they can count on.
byDistance.farAway: When we set dates for a trip home, I follow through — not endless "we'll see."

options.1: I often cancel, ghost on plans, or appear only when guilt spikes
options.2: I visit when it's convenient for me — they can't predict my rhythm
options.3: I show up sometimes but disappear for weeks without a word
options.4: I mostly keep planned visits or calls; when I slip, I reschedule clearly
options.5: They know my rhythm — I show up when I say I will, near or far

small-gestures.prompt: I do small practical things that say "I'm thinking of you" — not only on holidays.

options.1: Caring acts happen only on birthdays or holidays — otherwise silence
options.2: I mean to help but rarely follow through on small things
options.3: Occasional food, photos, or fixes when I'm there or reminded
options.4: Regular small acts — groceries, a link, fixing something on their phone
options.5: Small gestures are part of my week; they feel seen between big events

mark-dates.prompt: I remember and mark what matters to them — birthdays, yahrzeit, anniversaries, medical days.

options.1: I forget important dates or remember only after they're hurt
options.2: I remember late — a rushed text after the day passed
options.3: Reminders help; I usually acknowledge on the day
options.4: I mark key dates ahead and reach out with something personal
options.5: Their meaningful dates live on my calendar — honored consistently

quality-over-rush.prompt: When we're together, they get my attention — not only my phone and a rushed exit.

byDistance.sameArea: On local visits, I stay long enough for real talk — not a drive-by checklist.
byDistance.shortDrive: When I drive in, I protect unhurried time — not only errands and leave.
byDistance.farAway: On rare visits home, I'm present for conversations — not just scheduling the next flight out.

options.1: I'm on my phone or watching the clock — they feel like an interruption
options.2: I squeeze them in between tasks; warmth gets the leftovers
options.3: Some visits are rushed, some are good — depends on my week
options.4: I usually put devices away and leave room for unplanned conversation
options.5: They get unhurried time — I leave feeling connected, not just dutiful

invite-into-life.prompt: I invite them into my life — kids, work wins, ordinary Fridays — not only crises.

options.1: They hear from me mostly when I need something or when there's bad news
options.2: I share logistics (kids' schedules) but not much of my inner life
options.3: Sometimes I share photos or stories; often I forget to include them
options.4: I regularly loop them in — meals, milestones, small wins
options.5: They know my world ongoingly — inclusion is natural, not performative

follow-through-promises.prompt: When I promise "I'll call," "I'll fix that," or "I'll take you" — I follow through.

options.1: Promises slip constantly; they stop believing me
options.2: I follow through half the time — they're wary now
options.3: I try, but busy weeks mean broken promises without repair
options.4: I usually do what I say; when I can't, I say so early
options.5: My word is reliable — they don't have to chase me

help-without-being-asked.prompt: I notice what they need and help — without making them beg or feel like a burden.

byStage.independent: I offer help they might refuse — respectfully, without pushing my agenda.
byStage.someHelp: I step in on errands, appointments, or home tasks before they're exhausted asking.
byStage.caregiving: I share the load proactively — meds, nights, paperwork — not only when it boils over.

options.1: I wait until they ask loudly or until someone shames me into it
options.2: I help when reminded, often with sighs or delay
options.3: I help sometimes; other times I assume they're fine
options.4: I spot needs and offer concrete help — they can say no comfortably
options.5: Anticipating needs is normal for me — dignity stays intact

stay-in-touch-busy.prompt: When life gets loud, I still keep a thread with my parents — not radio silence.

byDistance.sameArea: Even in hectic weeks nearby, I send a text or knock — not weeks of absence.
byDistance.shortDrive: When I can't drive over, I still call or video — distance isn't an excuse for silence.
byDistance.farAway: Between trips, I keep contact steady — calls, photos — not disappearing until the next flight.

options.1: Busy seasons mean zero contact until someone guilt-trips me
options.2: A random text every few weeks — they feel like an afterthought
options.3: I touch base when I remember; gaps can stretch long
options.4: I keep a minimum rhythm even in chaos — short but real
options.5: They never wonder if I've forgotten them — thread stays alive

listen-without-fix.prompt: When they repeat a story or worry, I listen without immediately fixing or shutting them down.

options.1: I interrupt, correct, or say "you already told me"
options.2: I listen with one eye on my phone — they feel dismissed
options.3: I listen okay until I'm tired; then I rush them
options.4: I let stories breathe — I reflect before offering solutions
options.5: They feel heard even on repeat topics — patience is respect

ask-real-questions.prompt: I ask questions about their day, memories, and worries — not only yes/no check-ins.

options.1: Our talks are "everything fine?" and we move on
options.2: I ask surface questions but don't follow the thread
options.3: Sometimes a real question lands; often it's logistics
options.4: I regularly ask what matters to them and stay curious
options.5: Conversations go both ways — they feel interviewed with love, not audited

remember-details.prompt: I remember details they care about — names, doctors, neighbors, what they told me last time.

options.1: I forget what they said yesterday — they feel invisible
options.2: I remember big things only; small details slip
options.3: I remember when I write notes; otherwise it's hit or miss
options.4: I usually pick up threads from last call — "how did that go?"
options.5: They don't re-explain everything — I track what matters to them

patience-with-repeat.prompt: When they repeat themselves or move slowly, I stay patient — not sharp or mocking.

byStage.independent: When habits sound old-fashioned, I disagree without eye-rolls or public correction.
byStage.someHelp: When memory or hearing slips, I repeat calmly — not "I already said that."
byStage.caregiving: In long care days, I watch my tone — fatigue isn't their fault.

options.1: I snap, mock, or finish their sentences with irritation
options.2: Patience runs out fast — they feel like a nuisance
options.3: I'm patient sometimes; stress makes me sharp
options.4: I breathe before reacting — tone stays respectful
options.5: Slowness and repeats get grace — they feel safe with me

respect-their-pace.prompt: I respect their pace — meals, walks, decisions — without marching them like a project.

options.1: I rush them constantly — efficiency over dignity
options.2: I hurry visits; they feel managed, not met
options.3: Depends on my schedule — sometimes patient, sometimes pushy
options.4: I adjust to their tempo most of the time
options.5: Their pace sets the visit — I'm a guest in their rhythm

hear-worry-underneath.prompt: When they nag or criticize, I hear worry or loneliness underneath — not only the jab.

options.1: I fire back or go cold — every comment becomes war
options.2: I dismiss them as dramatic — miss the fear below
options.3: Sometimes I see the worry; often I take bait
options.4: I pause and ask what's really scaring them
options.5: I can translate nag into care — respond to the need, not the tone

disagree-with-honor.prompt: We can disagree — politics, parenting, money — without cutting them down.

options.1: Disagreement becomes contempt or silent punishment
options.2: I "win" arguments and leave them small
options.3: We avoid hot topics — connection thins
options.4: We disagree with boundaries — no name-calling, no dredging old wounds
options.5: Different views coexist — honor stays louder than debate

phone-call-presence.prompt: On phone or video, I'm actually there — not multitasking through their sentences.

byDistance.sameArea: Even when we could meet, phone calls get my full attention when we use them.
byDistance.shortDrive: On driving calls, I stay focused — or I call back when I can listen.
byDistance.farAway: Long-distance calls are main visits — I treat them like rooms, not background noise.

options.1: I'm cooking, driving distracted, or half-listening — they notice
options.2: Calls are short chores — "what do you need?"
options.3: Good calls mix with distracted ones
options.4: I usually stop other tasks for calls with them
options.5: They'd say I'm present on the line — voice, silence, and all

boundaries-without-cut.prompt: I can set limits (time, topics, visits) without cutting them off or punishing.

options.1: Boundaries mean silence, blocks, or dramatic exits
options.2: I say yes resentfully — then explode later
options.3: Limits are fuzzy — swing between over-giving and vanishing
options.4: I name limits kindly — "not tonight, yes Thursday"
options.5: Clear boundaries and warm connection coexist

guilt-managed.prompt: Guilt doesn't run the whole relationship — I act from choice, not only shame.

options.1: I avoid them because guilt is unbearable — or I overgive until I resent
options.2: Guilt drives big gestures then long disappearance
options.3: Guilt and love mix — some weeks better than others
options.4: I notice guilt, then choose a sane next step
options.5: I honor them without self-punishment — steady, not dramatic

own-family-balance.prompt: I balance my partner/kids and my parents — without making either side the villain.

options.1: Constant war — spouse vs. parents, kids caught inside
options.2: I hide visits or calls — sneakiness breeds shame
options.3: Balance wobbles; holidays are minefields
options.4: We negotiate time openly — some friction, some repair
options.5: Family roles are talked about — respect includes my household too

crisis-show-up.prompt: In health scares, falls, or loss — I show up practically and emotionally.

byStage.independent: When a scare hits, I'm there fast — hospital, calls to siblings — without taking over their agency.
byStage.someHelp: In ER nights or bad diagnoses, I coordinate and sit — not only send thoughts.
byStage.caregiving: In acute crises on top of daily care, I stabilize first — then breathe with them.

options.1: I freeze, argue with siblings, or disappear until it's over
options.2: Logistics only — no bedside or emotional presence
options.3: I show up unevenly — strong start, fade later
options.4: I'm reliably there for the hard hours — food, calls, holding hand
options.5: They know crisis means me — steady feet, open heart

no-scorekeeping.prompt: I don't keep a ledger of who did more — visits, money, calls — to justify pulling away.

options.1: I tally every sacrifice — weaponize it in fights
options.2: Silent scoreboard — resentment builds quietly
options.3: I scorekeep when stressed; let go when calm
options.4: I notice imbalance and talk — not prosecute
options.5: Giving isn't a deposit for withdrawal — respect flows

sibling-or-alone-load.prompt: If siblings share care — we talk load fairly; if I'm alone, I ask for help without martyrdom.

options.1: Sibling wars or solo martyrdom — nobody wins
options.2: I carry alone and explode at family group chat
options.3: Uneven load acknowledged but not fixed
options.4: We divide tasks or I hire/help openly
options.5: Load is named and shared — solo or with siblings

speak-needs-calmly.prompt: I can tell my parents what I need — time, tone, topics — calmly, not in a blow-up.

options.1: Needs come out as yelling or passive aggression
options.2: I swallow needs until I detonate
options.3: I hint; they don't understand; I give up
options.4: I say "I need…" in plain language, usually calm
options.5: Direct requests are normal — they can adjust without shame

humor-without-mock.prompt: We can laugh together — without sarcasm that slices or jokes at their expense.

options.1: Humor is mockery — they feel the sting
options.2: Jokes dodge real talk — laughter as escape
options.3: Warm humor sometimes; cutting humor sometimes
options.4: Inside jokes and lightness — never at their dignity
options.5: Laughter connects us — they feel teased with love, not targeted

accept-help-reversed.prompt: When they still want to give — food, money, advice — I receive with grace, not humiliation.

byStage.independent: When they insist on paying or hosting, I let them keep dignity — not a power fight.
byStage.someHelp: When help flows both ways, I accept without making them feel useless.
byStage.caregiving: Even as I care for them, I let them contribute small things that matter to them.

options.1: I refuse everything — they feel rejected and small
options.2: I take help then criticize — double message
options.3: Awkward either way — take or refuse without grace
options.4: I thank them and accept what keeps their pride
options.5: Receiving is respect too — their giving has a place

repair-after-friction.prompt: After tension or a harsh visit, I know how to repair — call, apology, or reset plan.

options.1: Bad visits linger — nobody reaches back
options.2: We pretend nothing happened — ice under the table
options.3: Someone softens eventually; no clear repair
options.4: I initiate repair — short call or "can we try again?"
options.5: Friction doesn't define us — we have a path back

protect-from-burnout.prompt: If I'm caregiving or very involved, I protect my floor — sleep, backup, respite — so respect stays sustainable.

byStage.independent: I don't borrow tomorrow's energy for guilt today — pace stays human.
byStage.someHelp: I schedule respite before I break — help is marathon, not sprint.
byStage.caregiving: I use backup, aides, or siblings — burnout helps no one.

options.1: Running on empty — irritable with them, ashamed with myself
options.2: No backup plan — white-knuckle until collapse
options.3: Some self-care; guilt calls it selfish
options.4: Regular breaks and help — respect includes me
options.5: Sustainable care — they get steadiness, not my wreckage

gratitude-spoken.prompt: I say thank you out loud — for sacrifices, recipes, babysitting, belief in me.

options.1: Gratitude stays unspoken — they guess or don't
options.2: Thanks only on big occasions — feels formal
options.3: I mean it; I forget to say it
options.4: I thank them for specific things regularly
options.5: Gratitude is spoken language in our relationship

future-care-talk.prompt: We've touched future care wishes — home, medical, money — without panic or avoidance.

byStage.independent: We talk wishes early — documents, values — while it's calm.
byStage.someHelp: We update plans as needs grow — who decides what, where.
byStage.caregiving: We revisit care plans honestly — changes, limits, dignity.

options.1: Taboo topic — fight or shut down if raised
options.2: Vague "we'll figure it out" — no specifics
options.3: One conversation; no follow-through
options.4: Some clear wishes and next steps documented
options.5: Ongoing, respectful planning — fear doesn't run the room

respect-their-autonomy.prompt: I respect their choices — even when I'd decide differently — unless true safety is at stake.

byStage.independent: I don't parent my parents — advice is offered once, not enforced.
byStage.someHelp: I support decisions they can still make — not only what eases my anxiety.
byStage.caregiving: Dignity of choice remains — bathroom, clothes, visitors — within safety.

options.1: I override them — "for your own good" becomes control
options.2: Nagging until they comply — autonomy erodes
options.3: Autonomy in easy areas; control when I'm scared
options.4: I consult them on big moves — their voice counts
options.5: Their life, their call — I walk beside, not on top
